events.title: A Wolf Shall Devour the Sun
events.blurb:
Respected by ancient cultures but the archetypal villain in European fairy tales, wolves were hunted to extinction in Scotland by the 18th century. Ancient myth, mesmeric imagery and dreamlike soundscapes open a liminal space where Norse gods, Irish shapeshifters and Siberian wolf-children traverse Scottish moors and Transylvanian mountains. Live music stirs the soul. Shadow puppetry and animation portray terror and playfulness. Stories about our oldest ally ask: in the absence of the wolf, what is lost?
Originally commissioned by the Scottish International Storytelling Festival 2024.
‘I was so mesmerised I had abandoned taking notes’ ★★★★★ (Snack)
‘Powerful and magical’ ★★★★ (List)
‘Richly textured’ ★★★★ (CorrBlimey.uk)
BSL interpreted Sun 9 Aug. Interpretation by Sarah Forrester

events.title: Michael Woods: Mount Everest Speaker
events.blurb:
Michael Woods is the first British Deaf person to summit Mount Everest, the highest mountain in the world. Over an eight-week expedition, he faced extreme weather, dangerous conditions, and physical exhaustion, all without the support of a BSL interpreter.
Communicating visually and through written notes with his expedition team, Michael overcame barriers that many thought impossible. In this inspiring and honest talk, he will share his remarkable journey of determination, resilience, and courage. Hear about the challenges he faced, the moments he nearly lost his life, and what it took to reach the summit.
Presentation will be delivered in BSL with English PowerPoint. BSL/English interpreters will be provided to ensure the event is accessible to both deaf and hearing audience members.
BSL

events.title: Watercolour Workshop with Vika Rudenko
events.blurb:
Join award-winning Deaf visual artist Viktoryia (Vika) Rudenko for a playful 2-hour exploration of
facial expression through watercolour and Deaf View/Image Art (De’VIA).
In Deaf culture, the eyes and mouth are essential tools of communication, conveying emotion,
tone, and meaning beyond words. Participants will paint expressive facial features using
pre-illustrated face templates while learning about De’VIA as a powerful form of Deaf artistic
and cultural expression.
All supplies are included, including watercolour paints, brushes, paper, and pre-illustrated facial
templates. No previous watercolour experience is required. All skill levels are welcome.

events.title: BSL Film Club x Edinburgh Deaf Festival
events.blurb:
As part of Edinburgh Deaf Festival, BSL Film Club will be hosting a special screening of Ted Evans’ Deaf-led thriller, Retreat .
The event will be introduced by BSL Film Club co-programmers, Tomas Gerrard and Charlie Little. There will also be a Q&A after the screening, with guests to be confirmed.
Retreat
Dir. Ted Evans
United Kingdom | 2025 | 107m | British Sign Language, English
In search of belonging and connection, a young woman arrives at a remote wellness retreat for Deaf people, but nothing is what it seems. A gripping debut thriller from filmmaker Ted Evans that will unsettle audiences and leave them guessing until the final frame.
Billed as the world’s first Deaf thriller and made in British Sign Language with an all-Deaf principal cast and a Deaf director, Retreat stars Anne Zander, Sophie Stone, and James Boyle.
Following the screening will be an accessible Q&A with local filmmaker and Solar Bear’s Film & Screen Lead Officer, Klarissa Webster.
Accessibility
BSL Film Club is an inclusive and accessible film club offering films with descriptive subtitles and open discussions in BSL after each screening.
All audiences with varying sign language fluency, both deaf and hearing, are welcome.
This film will be shown with descriptive subtitles (also known as captions).
This event will have BSL/English interpretation during the introduction and Q&A.
There will be English-language live captioning during the introduction and Q&A.
There is an external access lift for step-free access to the building. Once inside the building, there is a lift from the ground floor to the Blackwood Bar area, accessible on the left upon entry to the venue. Accessible toilets can also be found on the first floor. There is also lift access to the basement level. This screening will take place in the Blackwood Bar area.
This film is rated TBC
If you have any questions about the event, please contact Charlie Little at charlielittlefilm@gmail.com
Supported by Film Hub Scotland, part of the BFI’s Film Audience Network, awarding funding on behalf of Screen Scotland and the BFI National Lottery.

events.title: Exhibition Tour with Trudi Collier: Katie Paterson’s Afterlife
events.blurb:
Learn more about Collective Gallery’s summer programme at this BSL tour, designed for Deaf visitors.
Join us for a BSL Tour of Katie Paterson’s solo exhibition Afterlife. This Deaf-led tour will be hosted by Trudi Collier and will offer BSL visitors the opportunity to learn more about the exhibition. We will have refreshments to wrap up the session, with time to discuss the exhibition with Trudi, the Programme Team, and other attendees. Trudi will be joined by an interpreter for this event.
About Afterlife:
Originally commissioned for the Folkstone Triennial 2025, Afterlife will be shared with audiences in Scotland for the first time.
Afterlife is a sculptural installation comprised of nearly 200 amulets, each created with materials sourced from endangered landscapes and fragile ecosystems, exploring themes of deep time, geology, and the environment. Drawing on centuries of cultural and spiritual traditions to reflect the fragility of the natural world today, Afterlife prompts us to consider the legacies we leave for future generations.
Contains content related to the climate crisis.
This tour will be led in BSL and interpreted into English.
This event will take place in our Dome Gallery and outdoor Play Shelter, which has step-free access via our East Gate entrance. Please note that the outdoor paths leading to the gallery can become uneven and wet in harsh weather. Accessible toilet facilities, including baby change, are available at Collective Gallery.
You can find more access information about visiting Collective Gallery on our website. If you have any questions, please get in touch at +44 (0)131 556 1264 or email mail@collective-edinburgh.art.

events.title: Sign Language Poetry Workshop
events.blurb:
Interested in signed language poetry?
For the past 20 years, projects like the Deaf Poet’s Society and the ASL Slam in New York City have been an incubator of sign language poetry with the DEAF Community. Dana Callan-Farley, ASL performer and professor at Marquette University in the USA, offers to bring out the inner poet in you.
To become a “person of the eye” is to challenge how you “see” art. Using historical and contemporary examples, we will explore the relationship between signed language and visual vernacular, the art of performance and understanding. The goal? To help you find the inner visual poet that you are and create your own poem.
By employing ASL/BSL signs alongside a visual vernacular, the poet transforms into the message itself. Other poets play a crucial role as receivers and interpreters of the poetry being created. Each individual will perceive things uniquely and uncover various meanings, both concealed and clear, leading to distinct artistic interpretations.
This event is open to hearing and Deaf alike, young and old, new signer or expert signer – bring your open heart filled with poetry.
This event will be offered in English, American Sign Language and British Sign Language.

events.title: Dungeons & Deaf Dragons
events.blurb:
Our event is an inclusive, fully accessible tabletop roleplaying experience designed specifically for Deaf participants and BSL users. Using British Sign Language (BSL) as the primary mode of communication, the session invites players to step into a rich fantasy world through the use of pre-created characters, allowing both beginners and experienced players to join without barriers.
Participants will embark on immersive quests filled with exploration, problem-solving, and collaborative storytelling. Along the way, they may face intense battles against monsters or dragons, uncover hidden mysteries, and make meaningful choices that shape the outcome of the story. The experience blends creativity, strategy, and roleplay, encouraging communication, teamwork, and imagination within a Deaf-friendly environment.
Our goal is to create a welcoming space where Deaf individuals can engage fully in fantasy storytelling, express themselves through BSL, and enjoy a shared adventure that is both accessible and unforgettable.
BSL
IS

events.title: Lights & Lanterns
events.blurb:
Presented by Spectroscope, step inside our emporium of light and shadow, where history flickers to life and you become part of the spectacle. Try your hand at a 130 year old magic lantern, create your own hand painted glass slide, don a top hat, and transform into a Victorian projectionist guided by two enigmatic hosts from another era.
Inspired by the lives and work of deaf Victorian artists Harry Ash and Harry Bow, this immersive workshop draws on rich deaf archives and the lost art of shadowgraphy, storytelling through light, silhouette and movement.
Led by deaf performers David Ellington and Ciaran O’Breen, you will explore expressive techniques using your hands and body. Learn to shape shadows, invent your own signs, and create visual stories, whether solo or in collaboration with others.
Expect a playful, physical experience where past and present collide, and where light becomes language.

events.title: My Mother’s Spices and Ode to Seventeen: LumoTV Screening
events.blurb:
Warning: Ode to Seventeen contains frequent strong language and features intense themes related to mental health. Viewer discretion is advised.
A double-bill screening of two recent short films from Lumo TV.
My Mother’s Spices : After her mother is hospitalised, a deaf British-Sri Lankan woman returns to her quiet childhood home, where re-creating a sacred family recipe forces her to confront the cultural fractures and deep-rooted love that bind them together. Can the space between generations truly close, or will it always hold a silence only love can fill? Starring Ruchika Jain and Sankeetha Gathani and written and directed by Nadia Nadarajah, a Slick Films production for Lumo TV.
Ode to Seventeen : A vulnerable 17-year-old Hana waits at a London bus stop at midnight, grappling with her identity and a fading sense of safety. When an oddly familiar older woman joins her, a raw, emotional dialogue unfolds. Hana soon realises the stranger holding her together is her 27-year-old self. Together, across a decade of time, they begin to piece their broken selves back together like Kintsugi.

events.title: LumoTV Panel: Meet the Commissioners
events.blurb:
Lumo TV is the UK’s home of deaf entertainment and the world’s only sign language-led commissioning body, creating bold, accessible content that celebrates deaf and sign language communities. Formerly the British Sign Language Broadcasting Trust, Lumo TV commission across scripted, factual, entertainment and children’s programming, with a focus on authentic storytelling and developing deaf talent both on and off screen.
Joining this session will be factual commissioner Cathy Heffernan, and drama commissioner, Phillip Dodds. This is a chance to hear directly from Lumo TV’s commissioning team about what they’re looking for, how they work with creatives and how to approach them with ideas that feel both culturally authentic and creatively exciting.

events.title: BSL Tour – Earth Matters
events.blurb:
See soil through art. Earth Matters marks 300 years since the birth of James Hutton, the Edinburgh-born geologist, farmer and thinker who revolutionised our understanding of the ground beneath us.
Inspired by Hutton and subsequent trailblazers, 30 artists delve into this living ecosystem to reveal its brilliance, beauty and fragility.
This exhibition tour is in British Sign Language (BSL), led by Trudi Collier. Please book your ticket in advance and meet at the entrance to the exhibition in Inverleith House.
If you have any questions, please email creativeprogrammes@rbge.org.uk

events.title: Pray for Me
events.blurb:
Age Suitability :14+. This performance contains themes of religious trauma, ableism towards Deaf people, and cultural pressure within faith communities. References to emotional distress and prayer as “cure” are explored.
Live captioning will be available for the performance on Saturday 15 August.
Pray For Me, written and performed by Sarah Adedeji is a powerful new work-in-progress exploring faith, deafness and identity, as a Black Deaf woman confronts ideas of cure, belief and belonging through poetry, movement and live music by ISRA3L.
